 Best Car Accident Lawyers in Sacramento for 2026 
 November 16, 2026 
 Andrew Palmer 
 7 min read 
 A crash on Highway 50 or a side street in North Sacramento can leave you with medical bills, a damaged car and an adjuster calling before you have even seen a specialist. 
 Choosing a lawyer at that point is hard, because most firm websites say the same things. 
 This guide compares eight Sacramento firms that handle car and truck accident claims. 
 Each entry uses the same format so you can compare focus, office location and fee terms side by side, and every detail was checked against the firm’s own materials, State Bar records or attorney directories in November 2026. 
 Key Takeaways 
 Every firm on this list offers a free consultation, so you can speak with several before signing anything. 
 California requires contingency fee agreements to be in writing, and that agreement should explain fees and case costs. 
 Most injury lawsuits in California must be filed within two years, and claims against a public agency usually need an administrative claim within six months. 
 Language support, truck crash experience and who will actually handle your file are worth asking about at the first meeting. 
 Sacramento Car Accident Lawyers at a Glance 
 Firms compared: 8, all with offices in Sacramento 
 Typical fee model: contingency, with no attorney fee unless there is a recovery 
 First meeting: free consultation at every firm listed 
 Common practice areas: car accidents, truck accidents, motorcycle crashes and wrongful death 
 Bilingual service: English and Spanish listed by four firms 
 The 8 Best Car Accident Lawyers in Sacramento 
 1. Law Offices of J.G. Winter   
 Founding attorney Jeremy G. Winter has been licensed in California since 2006, and car and truck accidents sit at the center of the firm’s practice. Its reported settlements include USD 3.5 million in a commercial truck accident and USD 1.5 million in a car accident, and J.G. Winter Law offers full English and Spanish service backed by a Spanish-language website. 
 Best for: Spanish-speaking clients and big rig or commercial truck crashes 
 Office: 1540 River Park Dr, Suite 114A, Sacramento, CA 95815 
 Fees: Free consultation; contingency fee set out in a written agreement 
 2. Demas Law Group, P.C.   
 Founding partner John N. Demas has been licensed in California since 1992, and the firm represents injured people only. Its caseload covers car, truck and motorcycle crashes along with wrongful death claims, and its attorneys speak at legal education programs on car accident litigation. 
 Best for: Serious auto injury cases likely to need trial preparation 
 Office: 701 Howe Ave, Suite A-1, Sacramento, CA 95825 
 Fees: Free consultation; contingency fee 
 3. Law Offices of Edward A. Smith (AutoAccident.com)   
 Edward A. Smith opened his Sacramento personal injury practice in 1982 and runs AutoAccident.com, one of the longest-running accident information sites in California. The firm handles car, truck and motorcycle collisions, pedestrian injuries and wrongful death, and it advertises Spanish-language service. 
 Best for: Clients who want a long-established, accident-focused practice 
 Office: 1610 Arden Way, Suite 280, Sacramento, CA 95815 
 Fees: Free consultation; contingency fee 
 4. Dreyer Babich Buccola Wood Campora, LLP   
 This plaintiff injury firm is based in Sacramento and also has offices in San Jose, Carmel and San Juan Capistrano. Founding partner Robert A. Buccola is a Fellow of the American College of Trial Lawyers, and the firm’s lawyers handle auto accident, product liability and wrongful death claims. 
 Best for: Catastrophic injuries and cases with vehicle or product defect questions 
 Office: 20 Bicentennial Circle, Sacramento, CA 95826 
 Fees: Free consultation; contingency fee 
 5. Arnold Law Firm   
 Clayeo C. Arnold founded this firm in 1975 with one secretary and a law clerk, and it now represents injured people across the Sacramento region. Its accident practice includes car, truck and motorcycle crashes, and it accepts injury cases on a contingency basis. 
 Best for: Clients who want a large local firm with decades of trial history 
 Office: 865 Howe Ave, Sacramento, CA 95825 
 Fees: Free case evaluation; contingency fee 
 6. Eason & Tambornini, A Law Corporation   
 Established in 1996, this firm practices both personal injury and workers’ compensation law. That combination helps when a crash happens on the job, since a work-related collision can involve a comp claim and a third-party injury claim at the same time. 
 Best for: Work-related vehicle crashes and delivery or commercial drivers 
 Office: 1234 H Street, Suite 200, Sacramento, CA 95814 
 Fees: Free consultation; contingency fee 
 7. Moseley Collins Law   
 Moseley Collins Law reports more than 40 years of experience with injury victims and states that it has handled thousands of car accident cases, most in the Sacramento area. Its practice also covers truck crashes and medical malpractice, which can matter if treatment after a crash goes wrong. 
 Best for: Clients who want a high-volume car accident practice downtown 
 Office: 980 9th St, 16th Floor, Sacramento, CA 95814 
 Fees: Free consultation; contingency fee 
 8. Wyatt Law Corporation   
 Wyatt Law Corporation is a father-and-sons practice led by Raymond, Russ and Peter Wyatt, with additional offices in Yuba City and Fairfield. The firm handles car, truck, motorcycle and pedestrian accident claims for clients across Northern California. 
 Best for: Clients in Sacramento and the Yuba-Sutter or Solano areas 
 Office: 901 H St, Suite 601, Sacramento, CA 95814 
 Fees: Free consultation; contingency fee 
 Sacramento Car Accident Statistics 
 Sacramento’s roads carry more risk than those in most of California’s large counties. A Consumer Affairs analysis of NHTSA data, reported by the Sacramento Bee in July 2024, found that Sacramento County recorded 13.6 traffic deaths per 100,000 residents in 2022, the fourth highest among the state’s 10 most populous counties. The city’s rate of 14.7 per 100,000 was the highest of any large California city. 
 The same analysis named the county’s deadliest roads for 2020 through 2022: 
 Interstate 5: 28 deaths 
 Highway 99: 27 deaths 
 Highway 160: 21 deaths 
 Highway 50: 20 deaths 
 Statewide, the California Office of Traffic Safety reports that NHTSA estimated a 6.3% decline in traffic deaths in 2024 compared with 2023. Even with that drop, four of the county’s five deadliest roads in the 2020 to 2022 analysis were state highways or interstates.

 What to Ask Before You Hire a Car Accident Lawyer 
 A free consultation is your chance to test fit, not just to hear a pitch. Ask who will handle your file day to day, how often you will get updates, and whether the firm has taken cases like yours to trial. 
 Ask for the fee agreement in writing before you sign. California law requires contingency agreements to be written, and the document should explain the fee percentage, how case costs are handled and what happens if there is no recovery. 
 Be careful with quick offers from the other driver’s insurer. As this breakdown of early settlement offers explains, a fast offer often arrives before you know what future treatment and lost income will cost, and a signed release usually ends the claim. 
 How This List Was Put Together 
 Firms were selected based on a Sacramento office, a stated focus on car and truck accident claims, free consultations and contingency fee representation. 
 Founding dates, licenses, addresses and service details were checked against firm websites, State Bar of California records and established attorney directories in November 2026. 
 The order reflects fit for car and truck crash claims and language access. It is not a ranking of case outcomes, and past results never guarantee a future result. 
 Conclusion 
 The right Sacramento car accident lawyer depends on your injuries, the vehicles involved and how you want to communicate. 
 Use the free consultations, compare the written fee terms and choose the firm whose lawyers explain your options clearly. 
 Frequently Asked Questions 
 How long do I have to file a car accident lawsuit in California? 
 Most personal injury lawsuits must be filed within two years of the injury under Code of Civil Procedure section 335.1. 
 What if a city or county vehicle caused the crash? 
 You usually need to file an administrative claim with the public agency within six months under Government Code section 911.2. 
 Do I have to report a crash to the DMV? 
 Yes, file an SR-1 within 10 days if anyone was injured or killed or if property damage was more than USD 1,000. 
 Can I recover money if I was partly at fault? 
 Yes, California follows pure comparative fault, so your award is reduced by your share of responsibility. 
 How much does a Sacramento car accident lawyer cost? 
 Most work on contingency, so you pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery, with terms set out in a written agreement.
